thesis_statement: Eli Lilly owns the incretin franchise (Mounjaro + Zepbound) at global scale: 48% revenue growth on 60% volume, raised guidance, retatrutide's complete Phase 3 obesity package ready for a Q1 2027 BLA, and $4.5B of additional Indiana manufacturing to serve demand it still cannot fully supply.

base.summary: Revenue grows 35-40% through 2026 as supply comes online, international Mounjaro volumes keep compounding, and price erosion stays manageable against volume.
drivers: Mounjaro and Zepbound volume (+60% total volume growth)
retatrutide obesity BLA submission in Q1 2027

bull.summary: Retatrutide approval opens the next demand wave (obesity, sleep apnea, knee osteoarthritis) before any meaningful GLP-1 price war, and orforglipron's oral convenience expands the total market.
drivers: retatrutide Phase 3 package complete for three indications
orforglipron U.S. submission for type 2 diabetes filed

bear.summary: GLP-1 competition and price erosion arrive faster than the pipeline monetizes: realized prices fell 13% in the quarter (U.S. -3%, ex-U.S. -36% on China NRDL), and a ~40x trailing multiple de-rates on any volume-growth deceleration.
drivers: intensifying incretin competition (oral orforglipron peers, biosimilars)
IPR&D spend ($3.03/share in Q2) and acquisition integration risk

key_risks: Price erosion is real and accelerating outside the U.S. (-36% realized, China NRDL) and emerging in the U.S. (-3%, or ~-9% excluding rebate adjustments); the thesis needs volume growth to keep outrunning it.
Valuation: ~39.7x trailing and ~24.9x forward prices in continued dominance; forward ~25x is reasonable only if the growth persists.
Concentration: the incretin franchise dominates revenue; a safety signal or supply failure in Mounjaro/Zepbound is a franchise-level event.
Q2 EPS ($7.94 reported) includes $3.03 of acquired IPR&D charges - judge underlying non-GAAP ($8.38) and the raised revenue guidance, not the GAAP line.
